metrics.name: stops_completed
metrics.description: Delivery stops completed, as Amazon's itinerary summary counts them; the station pickup is not a stop.

metrics.name: packages_delivered
metrics.description: Packages delivered, as Amazon's itinerary summary counts them.

metrics.name: packages_remaining
metrics.description: Packages not yet delivered or returned when the day was collected.

metrics.name: break_minutes
metrics.description: Break time Amazon recorded on the itinerary.

metrics.name: overtime_minutes
metrics.description: Overtime Amazon recorded on the itinerary.

metrics.name: days_worked
metrics.description: Days with hours on the Paycom timecard.

metrics.name: lunch_minutes
metrics.description: Minutes between Paycom's lunch out and lunch in punches.

metrics.name: clock_in
metrics.description: First clock in, in the DSP's time.

metrics.name: clock_out
metrics.description: Last clock out, in the DSP's time.

metrics.name: meal_issues
metrics.description: Days the meal-break comparison found something to look at, among the days the driver had a Cortex route.

metrics.name: meal_status
metrics.description: The meal-break comparison's verdict; see the glossary.

metrics.name: inspections
metrics.description: Recorded short DVIC exceptions; alias of short_inspections.

metrics.name: short_inspections
metrics.description: DVIC inspections shorter than their minimum.

glossary.meaning: A six-character code for one person, the same across every source. Use it to name a driver exactly.
Amazon's ID for a driver across its data sources.
Sunday to Saturday, named by the ISO week of its Saturday, as 2026-W39.
When the driver left the station to start the route, in the DSP's time.
When the route's session ended, after the last stop.
A route day collected while it was still in progress; numbers can still change.
Daily Vehicle Inspection Checklist, done before driving. Inspections under their minimum (90 or 300 seconds by vehicle) count as short.
Cortex's meal break and Paycom's lunch punches agree.
They disagree by more than the allowed difference.
Cortex has a meal break; Paycom has no lunch punches.
Paycom has lunch punches; Cortex has no meal break. With cortexRoute false, Cortex had no route for the person, so no meal break was expected there.
Only Cortex has the driver that day.
Paycom's punches don't read as a whole day.
Meal breaks and lunches don't pair up one to one.
A source has nothing for the driver yet.
